# Environment variables

Every `AIO_*` variable the framework reads, in one table — because a variable
that works and is documented nowhere is a feature only its author can use. A
field report found `AIO_BUILD_VERSION` by reading aio's build source.

`deno task check:env` fails when `src/` reads a variable this page does not
name, so the table cannot fall behind the code.

Examples in these docs set one inline, POSIX style (`AIO_X=1 deno task dev`). In
PowerShell that is `$env:AIO_X = '1'; deno task dev` —
[more spellings](../basics/windows-macos.md#powershell-for-the-posix-snippets).

## Running an app

| Variable                   | Read by           | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AIO_PORT`                 | boot              | Port to serve on. `--port` wins over it; both win over `port:` in config. Not read by an Electron client whose app sets [`electron: { ignoreDebugEnv: true }`](../clients/electron.md)                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `AIO_DEFAULT_PORT`         | boot              | Port to serve on when nothing else names one — below `--port`, `AIO_PORT` and `port:` in config, instead of a random free port. The generated systemd unit sets it to `3000`. Ignored like `AIO_PORT` under `electron: { ignoreDebugEnv: true }`                                                                                                                  |
| `AIO_MOVE_TO_APPLICATIONS` | macOS desktop app | `never` — do not offer to move the app into Applications; `move` — move it without asking. Unset: ask once (see [targets](targets.md#build-targets))                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `AIO_HOME`                 | installers, `am`  | Where aio itself lives (checkout or install root)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `AIO_PROFILE`              | boot              | Run from this profile's data home — the env form of `--profile=<name or path>`; the flag wins. Refused under `profiles: false` (see [profiles](../clients/app-manager.md#profiles-several-copies-of-one-app))                                                                                                                                                     |
| `AIO_APPS_DIR`             | app dirs          | Root for every app's data directory — the one switch that moves all of them (see [where files live](../persistence/where-files-live.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `AIO_INSTALL_ROOT`         | installs          | Where an installed app lives (`am installed` lists them). Default `~/app/<name>/`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `AIO_TEST_ROOT`            | tests             | Root for every directory the test harnesses create. Default `~/tmp/aio/`, mode 0700 — user space, not `/tmp`: a test's scratch holds an `auth.db`, an `app.key` and TLS material                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `AIO_APPS_SANDBOX`         | tests             | Set by the test harness, never by hand: the `apps-<pid>` dir under `AIO_TEST_ROOT` it made for `AIO_APPS_DIR` — one per process, shared by its test files and removed by the last; an `AIO_APPS_DIR` that differs from it is a runner's own pin and is left alone                                                                                                 |
| `AIO_VERSIONS_DIR`         | framework pin     | Where pinned aio versions are kept                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `AIO_UPDATE_CHANNEL`       | update check      | Follow a different channel than the one stamped into the artifact                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `AIO_PARENT_PID`           | Electron child    | The pid the window (and a supervised app) must not outlive — set by the launcher, not by hand. Decimal digits only; a hex/exponent/signed spelling is treated as unset                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `AIO_LOCK_HANDOFF`         | `am start` child  | The one-time secret that lets the app take over the lock `am start` held while it spawned it — set by `am`, not by hand                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `AIO_APP_CWD`              | Electron child    | The app's working directory, for the window's main script — set by the launcher, not by hand. An installed app's window runs from the Windows directory, so that the install folder can be moved by an update                                                                                                                                                     |
| `AIO_STDOUT_IS_LOG=1`      | console           | This process's stdout is a log file (`am start` sets it: `logs/stdout.log`) — the share-link token and pair code are masked there, as in every log file                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `AIO_NO_OPEN=1`            | `open-external`   | Never open a browser or a file manager. For any harness that must not spawn a UI                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `AIO_AM_DISPLAY`           | `am start`        | Where a started app's window goes when `--display=` is not given: `auto` (default — no human on the terminal → a nested display, tabs suppressed), `isolated`, `current`, or `:N`. Anything else is refused                                                                                                                                                       |
| `AIO_DISCOVERY_PORT`       | discovery         | UDP port apps broadcast and answer discovery probes on — server and client must match. Default `8099` (see [the Electron client](../clients/electron.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `AIO_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS`    | packaged window   | How long the Electron main process waits for the app to ANSWER a request over its socket or named pipe before it gives the window a 504 saying which request timed out. Default `30000`. Decimal digits only (hex/exponent/signed → default). Bounded to the first byte only — a stream that goes quiet after its headers (SSE, a long download) is never cut off |
| `AIO_SUPERVISED=1`         | restart decision  | "You are supervised: exit, do not spawn your own successor" — the generated systemd unit sets it (see [updates](../deploy/updates.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `AIO_STOP_STAYS_DOWN=1`    | restart decision  | With `AIO_SUPERVISED=1`: `am stop` exits 143, as `aio.stop()` does, so the supervisor leaves the app down. Unset, `am stop` exits 0 and `Restart=always` starts it again. The generated launchd agent and Windows task script set it; the systemd unit has it as a comment (see [updates](../deploy/updates.md))                                                  |
| `AIO_DEV_SUPERVISED=1`     | dev restart       | Set on the child by the dev auto-restart supervisor: the child exits with code 75 instead of spawning its own successor, and the supervisor relaunches it (see [dev mode](dev-mode.md))                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `AIO_DEV_RESTART_PORT`     | dev restart       | Set on the child by the dev auto-restart supervisor, never by hand: the TCP port the app was on, so the relaunched app binds the same one. Read only together with `AIO_DEV_SUPERVISED=1`; it is not `AIO_PORT`, so [`electron: { ignoreDebugEnv: true }`](../clients/electron.md) does not take it out                                                           |
| `AIO_DEV_RESTART_SAVED`    | dev restart       | Set on the child by the dev auto-restart supervisor, never by hand: which source files the last start already found saved (a count and hashes). A file the app's own start writes each time is then not taken for an edit made while the app was starting. Read only together with `AIO_DEV_SUPERVISED=1`                                                         |
| `AIO_NO_DEV_RESTART=1`     | dev restart       | Opt OUT of the dev auto-restart: a saved file no longer relaunches the app, so a crash or a syntax error stays on screen instead of looping                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `AIO_MAX_HEAP_MB`          | tests, `am start` | Cap every app's V8 heap ceiling at this many MB. The release suite sets it to the 4 GB floor so the many apps it spawns cannot each inherit 25% of a large host's RAM and exhaust the machine. Never below the 4 GB floor; unset in production. See [where code runs](../basics/where-code-runs.md)                                                               |

## Building

| Variable                  | Read by                       | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AIO_BUILD_VERSION`       | build                         | **The supported way a parent build hands a version to a child.** See below                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `AIO_BUILD_COMMIT`        | update check                  | The commit a build came from, when git is not available where the binary runs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `AIO_PROBE_NONCE`         | `--aio-data-contract`         | Set by `ship` / `am publish` / the git update source when they ask a binary for its data contract — not by hand. The binary prints its answer lines as `[aio:<value>] …` instead of `[aio] …`, so nothing the app itself prints can pass for one                                                                                                                                                               |
| `AIO_BUILD_PROBE`         | android / web build           | Set to `1` in the process where the build runs your entry module once to read its `aio.run()` options — not by hand. That process can only read (no write, network or subprocess). An entry reads it to skip top-level work during a build. See [Runtime differences](runtime-differences.md#a-packaged-apk-never-runs-appts)                                                                                  |
| `AIO_BUILD_NOTES`         | build                         | Set by `deno task build` for each target it builds — not by hand: the file a target's build writes its advisories to (an `icon.png` Windows cannot use, a one-click `.exe` left without an icon), so the closing summary repeats them. Unset, they are only warned where they happen                                                                                                                           |
| `AIO_ELECTRON_PROTOCOL=1` | dev                           | Load the dev window over `aio://` — the packaged path — instead of `http://`. Test what you ship                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `AIO_ELECTRON_SANDBOX=1`  | Electron                      | Force the strict sandbox behaviour rather than the platform default                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `AIO_ELECTRON_ARGS=…`     | Electron                      | Extra Chromium switches, space separated (`--disable-gpu --disable-dev-shm-usage`). An ALLOW-list — the display/GPU/locale/logging set; anything else (`--remote-debugging-port`, `--js-flags`, …) is refused and named in the log with its reason. See docs/clients/electron.md                                                                                                                               |
| `AIO_MACOS_SSH`           | macOS build                   | `[user@]mac-host` reachable over SSH with `hdiutil`, so a Linux/Windows host can produce a macOS `.dmg`: the `.app` is shipped there, imaged, and fetched back. Equivalent to `"build": { "macos": { "host": … } }`. See docs/build/targets.md                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `AIO_STRIP_CHROMIUM=1`    | Electron package              | Strip the optional Chromium extras — `dxcompiler.dll`/`dxil.dll` and all of Vulkan: the software implementation and the loader (`vulkan-1.dll`, `libvulkan.so.1`) — from the packaged runtime. The env form of `"build": { "chromiumExtras": "strip" }`. WebGL, media (`ffmpeg`), ICU data and every license file are never candidates. See [targets](targets.md#optional-chromium-extras-buildchromiumextras) |
| `AIO_SKIP_TRIM=1`         | compile                       | Keep source maps, docs and test-fixture directories in the compiled binary. They are otherwise held aside for the compile (and restored afterwards) because no runtime path reads them. For a build you are debugging. See [targets](targets.md)                                                                                                                                                               |
| `AIO_WINDOWS_FAT_EXE=1`   | Windows build                 | Emergency rollback for the Windows `.exe`: build the legacy fat self-contained PE that embeds Electron's release zip in Deno's VFS, instead of the default zip-sized SFX (stub + zstd tar payload). Download is ~2× larger; offline double-click is unchanged. The build falls back to it by itself, with a warning, when the stub cannot be read, fetched or verified                                         |
| `ELECTRON_PATH`           | Electron                      | Use this Electron runtime instead of the downloaded one                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `ELECTRON_MIRROR`         | Electron                      | Mirror to download Electron from                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `AIO_SHARED_ELECTRON_DIR` | shared-runtime app            | Where the [shared Electron store](targets.md#shared-electron-runtime-buildelectronruntime) is, instead of the per-user app-data folder                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `AIO_DIALOG`              | shared-runtime app            | `none` — no progress window or Retry/Quit question while Electron downloads (the log carries both); `browser` — on Linux, the browser page instead of zenity/yad                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `AIO_ELECTRON_RUNTIME`    | updater                       | Set by a shared-runtime AppImage's `AppRun`, not by hand: `shared:<its mount>`, so the updater knows the install is an Electron AppImage that carries no Electron                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `AIO_AVD`                 | `dev-android`, `test:android` | Which Android emulator image to boot. Default: the first one                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `AIO_ANDROID_KEYSTORE`    | Android `--release`           | Your release keystore (a path, relative to the app root or absolute). With it a release build is signed, not debuggable, and also writes the `.aab`. Needs `AIO_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` and `AIO_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS`; `AIO_ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` when the key has its own. Read by Gradle from the environment — never written to a file. See [targets](targets.md#signing-a-release-apk--aab)               |
| `AIO_ANDROID_SERIAL`      | `test:android`                | Run the Android lane on this attached device (a phone) instead of an emulator; the proof row is then `android (device)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `AIO_PLAYWRIGHT_DIR`      | `test:webkit`                 | A directory where `npm i playwright` and `npx playwright install webkit` were run. The WebKit lane drives that engine; without it the lane is skipped and says so. Nothing is downloaded by a test                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

### `AIO_BUILD_VERSION` — one build, one version

aio derives a version rather than accepting one: `deno.json` `version` plus the
repository's commit count, with `-dirty.<hash>` when the tree is not clean. That
is right for a build that owns its repository and wrong for a build that is a
**child** of another one.

The case that matters: a build script that rewrites tracked files before
building (baking in a key or a CA, restoring the placeholder afterwards). aio's
builder, running inside that window, sees a dirty tree and stamps
`0.2.4-dirty.f0bfee54` into an artifact whose file name and signed manifest both
say `0.2.4` — three derivations of one number, disagreeing.

```sh
# The parent decides once; every child build carries that exact string.
AIO_BUILD_VERSION=0.2.4 deno task build
```

`buildVersionFor` returns it verbatim — no re-derivation, no dirty suffix. This
is how aio's own fleet hands one version to its per-target children, and it is
the supported hand-off for any parent build.

## Diagnostics and tests

| Variable                    | Read by                         | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AIO_DEBUG=1`               | `deno task ship`                | Keep the stack trace on a ship error that would otherwise print one line and exit                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `AIO_DEV`                   | `install.sh`                    | Marks a development checkout so `am upgrade` leaves it alone                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `AIO_AM_NO_DELEGATE=1`      | `am`                            | Do not delegate to the app's pinned aio — run this `am`                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `AIO_CDP=1`                 | app                             | Open a CDP port so `am shot` can attach. Ignored by an app that sets `electron: { ignoreDebugEnv: true }` — pass `--cdp` instead                                                                                                                                                  |
| `AIO_TEST_NAMES=all`        | `testUI`                        | Print every semantic name the harness resolved, not just the misses                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `AIO_TEST_WIRE=strict`      | `testUI`                        | Every mount of the run crosses the wire for a rejection, a `serverFn` call and `useAio().send` (`wire: { strict: true }` on a mount decides for that mount). `am create` writes it into a new app's `test` task (see [UI testing](../testing/ui-testing.md#calls-cross-the-wire)) |
| `AIO_TEST_BROWSER_HOME=own` | `testBrowser`, `testUI --video` | Linux: the headless Chromium gets a HOME inside its throwaway profile, so its crash database and NSS store are not written under yours; your fonts and fontconfig rules are still found. Unset, the browser runs in your HOME                                                     |
| `AIO_TEST_DISPLAY`          | test helper                     | Set by the test display helper; tells `open-external` it is inside a harness                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `AIO_TEST_PORT_SLICE`       | `freePort()`                    | `first-last`: hand out test ports only from this range. Set per process by the parallel test runner, so two processes never get the same port                                                                                                                                     |
| `AIO_VIDEO`                 | `testUI`                        | Record each `testUI` test as a video: a directory (one file per test) or one `.mp4`/`.webm` file. The env form of `--video=`                                                                                                                                                      |
| `AIO_VIDEO_PACE`            | `testUI`                        | Milliseconds each step stays on screen in that video (default 800, 50–60000). The env form of `--video-pace=`; refused without a video                                                                                                                                            |
| `AIO_VIDEO_SCHEME`          | `testUI`                        | `light` or `dark`: the `prefers-color-scheme` the video is drawn in (default light). The env form of `--video-scheme=`                                                                                                                                                            |
| `AIO_FEEDBACK_DIR=…`        | `am feedback`                   | Where findings about aio are written. Defaults to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/aio/feedback` — OUTSIDE the versioned directory, so an upgrade cannot delete them                                                                                                                               |

## Not aio's

Read, never set: `HOME`, `USER`, `USERPROFILE`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `APPDATA`,
`TMPDIR`/`TEMP`/`TMP`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`,
`DISPLAY`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, `CI`, `ANDROID_HOME`, `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`,
`JAVA_HOME`, `CHROME_BIN`, `CHROMIUM_BIN`, `APPIMAGE`, `APPDIR`, `ARGV0`.

`TMPDIR` deserves a note: it decides where an AppImage unpacks itself, and it is
read by the AppImage runtime **before** your app starts — see
[targets](targets.md#appimage-and-tmpdir).
